comments.author: @RafBo-d3u
comments.text:
Horrible country, the most expensive place in south America, if it is such a wonderful place why people are leaving by the thousands. Montevideo is on its way to look rundown like Cuba, full of old people and old buildings in a terrible state of disrepair...!!! 

Don't waste your time going there, the only place that was worth visiting 30 years ago was Punta del Este for it's natural and deserted beaches, they have all been ruined now by cheap and ugly real estate developments that have ruined completely the cost line with uncontrolled overbuilding, in part, due to money laundering projects and other shady investments that park their money there. 

The food is also absolutely pathetic, go at your own risk, a Chivito cost up to 7 dollars and it taste like disécate stored meat...!!! there are hundreds of places worth visiting before entering that disappearing socialist failed state. I have been to Uruguay 22 times due to work obligations, going to that country has always been a horrible experience, you cannot wait to leave that place. 

I will also define Uruguay as the most BORRING country in the world, there is just nothing to do there. Turism is just not possible there, because outside of the capital there is almost nothing to see or to do there, just a bunch of poor and collapsing little towns with nothing to offer. I rather visit the Sahara desert during a hot summer month than go there, at least I would get to pet a camel, anything would be better then having to go back to that sh#thole of a country... You have been warned...!!!

comments.author: @GlobalJourNey-8386
comments.text: The salary tells only half the story. If two people earn the same amount but one owns a home and the other pays rent, their lives could be completely different. In Uruguay, what’s hardest to afford on this wage: housing, groceries, or transport?

replies.author: @shaileshsurin7133
replies.text: Great point about owning vs renting, it changes everything. I'm not from Uruguay, but from what I've read, housing is usually the biggest burden, especially renting in Montevideo, where rent can take a huge chunk of an average salary. Groceries are also known to be pricey compared to neighboring countries. Would love to hear from someone who actually lives there though!
